questions.title: Which senior Chinese official will hold talks with Jo Yong Won in Pyongyang in the first half of July 2026?
questions.background: Jo Yong Won is a senior official in North Korea's governing Workers' Party. Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June 2026 as Beijing and Pyongyang sought closer ties.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : KCNA, as reported by Reuters, identifying the senior Chinese official holding talks with Jo Yong Won in Pyongyang between July 1 and July 15, 2026, inclusive. Resolution Date : 2026-07-16 Accepted Answer Format : string (name). Answer with the Chinese official's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Significant 2026-07-11 update from Yonhap (19:01 KST), Korea Times, Straits Times/Reuters, and Xinhua marking the actual July 11 65th anniversary of the 1961 China-DPRK Treaty. Premier Li Qiang (previously 0.13) met visiting DPRK Premier Pak Thae-song IN BEIJING on Saturday July 11 (following Xi Jinping's Friday meeting and PSC #5 Cai Qi's Friday reception keynote, plus Xi-Kim congratulatory letters on July 11). Combined with Li Qiang already having led China's delegation to Pyongyang in October 2025, Saturday's Beijing bilateral talks virtually eliminate Li Qiang from flying to Pyongyang for July 12-15 talks with Jo Yong Won (dropping him out of the top 5 to ~0.02). Furthermore, the July 11 treaty anniversary passed without a simultaneous Chinese PSC delegation arriving in Pyongyang, shifting weight away from a pure treaty-day premier swap toward either (a) a staggered post-visit PSC envoy who has not visited Pyongyang recently and had no July 10-11 Beijing hosting role—Executive Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang (held at 0.16, matching both PSC rank and the 2011 Vice Premier Zhang Dejiang precedent) and CPPCC Chair Wang Huning (0.14 -> 0.13, top socialist-bloc ideological envoy)—or (b) a direct party-to-party delegation visiting July 12-14 specifically to hold talks with WPK Presidium Secretary and OGD chief Jo Yong Won, elevating Politburo/Secretariat member and CPC Central Organization Department head Shi Taifeng (0.11 -> 0.14, Jo Yong Won's exact institutional counterpart) and bringing IDCPC Minister Liu Haixing (who accompanied Xi to Pyongyang in June 2026 and runs CPC-WPK liaison) back into the top 5 at 0.11. Proven April 2024 Pyongyang envoy Zhao Leji trims slightly (0.09 -> 0.075, lower due to recent repeat and legislative-track role). Top-5 sum = 0.615, preserving 38.5% across Li Xi, Liu Guozhong, Li Hongzhong, Wang Yi, Cai Qi, Zhang Guoqing, He Lifeng, Li Qiang, and other senior officials.

questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
questions.background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Qualifying Event : Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify. Source of Truth : Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the state.
questions.current_reasoning: July 1-3 reporting (Cliff Daily, New Pine Plains Herald, Highlands Current) confirms New York's Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642/A11560, passed Senate 44-16 and Assembly 102-39 on June 4) has still not been formally delivered to Gov. Kathy Hochul, which policy analysts read as active chapter-amendment negotiations signaling Hochul is likely to sign a narrowed version (higher MW threshold/in-progress carve-outs, still qualifying as a statewide moratorium on large new hyperscale data centers) rather than issue an outright veto. Progressive NY primary victories and early-July heatwave power-conservation alerts further raise election-year pressure on Hochul ahead of November, while no competing state passed a statewide construction moratorium through July 6 (VA/FL/IL July 1 measures were tax/tariff/incentive policies; MN and MI actions remain municipal only; Maine's bill was already vetoed with override failed). Raising New York from 0.74 to 0.79 (retaining ~21% veto/collapse/other-state risk) and reallocating secondary slots to active full-time legislatures (Michigan 0.04, Pennsylvania 0.03, California 0.03, New Jersey 0.02; 9% residual).

questions.title: Who will win stage 11 of the 2026 Tour de France?
questions.background: The Tour de France awards individual stage victories separately from the overall race title.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The race organizer’s official stage 11 classification, corroborated by contemporaneous reputable sports reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the rider officially classified as the winner of stage 11 of the 2026 Tour de France, including any penalties applied when the stage results are confirmed. Accepted Answer Format : The winning rider’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-11 Stage 8 Bergerac pure bunch-sprint evidence (Cyclingnews, BBC Sport, AP, Reuters/Straits Times): (1) Tim Merlier (Soudal Quick-Step) won back-to-back flat sprints despite being boxed in around 7th-10th wheel entering the final 400m without lead-out man Bert Van Lerberghe, unleashing untouchable raw straight-line speed to sweep past rivals (now 3rd, 1st, 1st across all three 2026 Tour flat sprints). With Stage 9 (July 12) shortened by 30km due to the Correze heatwave red alert and a July 13 rest day reducing sprinter attrition ahead of Stage 11's wide, descending Vichy-to-Nevers boulevard, Merlier rises sharply as clear favorite (0.24 -> 0.29, ~33% conditional share given ~87% bunch-sprint probability). (2) Biniam Girmay (NSN) surged again to 2nd (half a bike length behind Merlier), improving 6th -> 3rd -> 2nd across the three flat sprints and beating Philipsen twice straight; he overtakes Philipsen into #3 (0.09 -> 0.13). (3) Stage 5 winner Olav Kooij bounced back from Stage 7's 23rd to finish 3rd cleanly, confirming health, though trimmed (0.20 -> 0.17) as Merlier and Girmay outpaced him. (4) Jasper Philipsen finished 4th (5th, 5th, 4th across pure sprints) despite another textbook Mathieu van der Poel lead-out, nudged 0.11 -> 0.10. (5) Max Kanter faded to 9th after XDS Astana led through the final corner (still best #5 flat-sprint profile at 2nd, 4th, 9th vs Waerenskjold 11th, Pedersen 12th, Bittner 5th), trimmed 0.06 -> 0.04. Residual 27% reflects ~13% breakaway/non-sprint risk (Liam Slock nearly held off the peloton until 1.3km on Stage 8) plus ~14% field sprinters (Bittner, Waerenskjold, Ackermann, Pedersen, Fretin, Meeus, Bauhaus) and Stage 9-10 crash/heat attrition.

local_articles.title: Tour de France Stage 9 shortened amid heatwave
local_articles.snippet: Bergerac – Tour de France organisers for the first time in the race’s history have decided to shorten a stage due to intense heat. Just minutes after the 33-year-old Belgian Tim Merlier had surged to victory in the 180km Stage 8 run from Perigueux to Bergerac with a stunning dash for the line on July 11, ASO announced that Stage 9 on July 12 would be changed because of a red alert in the central Correze region. Meteo France, the country’s weather authority, had declared a red alert “due to an exceptionally intense heatwave” in Correze, ASO said in a statement. ASO have shaved 30km off the 185.5km stage from Malemort to Ussel, cutting out a hilly loop at the beginning of the stage. “This decision has been made necessary by the exceptional weather conditions,” said ASO. “It aims to ensure that the race can take place under conditions compatible with the red heatwave alert.” Tour director C
